did_you_know.text: Did you know? The first message in Haggai chapter 2 was delivered on the twenty-first day of the seventh month through the prophet Haggai.
Did you know? Haggai addresses those who saw the First Temple and compares its glory with the appearance of the Temple being built at that time.
Did you know? The command to be strong is addressed to Zerubbabel, Joshua the high priest, and all the people of the land—and it is accompanied by the promise: “I am with you.”
Did you know? Haggai reminds the people of the covenant the LORD made with them when they came out of Egypt, and adds that His Spirit remains among them; therefore, they are told not to be afraid.
Did you know? The prophecy says that the LORD will shake all the nations, and afterward the Temple will be filled with glory.
Did you know? In the promise concerning the Temple’s glory, it says: “The silver is mine and the gold is mine”—a declaration emphasizing that wealth belongs to the LORD.
Did you know? Haggai declares that the future glory of the latter Temple will be greater than the glory of the former Temple, and that peace will be given in this place.
Did you know? In the priests’ answer to Haggai’s question, holy meat does not make other foods holy merely because it touched them through the hem of a garment.

Did you know? By contrast, according to the priests’ answer, contact with someone who is ceremonially unclean through contact with the dead makes food unclean; Haggai uses this distinction to describe the people’s condition and actions before the LORD.
Did you know? At the end of the chapter, the LORD declares Zerubbabel His chosen servant and compares him to a “signet ring”—a personal object kept close to its owner.
